recipes.name: Bauernomlett (Farmer's Omelet)
ingredients_raw: 3 slices bacon, cut into 1/2 inch pieces

steps.text: Place potatoes in a saucepan covered by lightly salted water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to medium, and simmer until tender, 10 to 15 minutes. Drain and allow to cool, then cut into 1/4-inch slices.

Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the bacon strips in the butter until browned, 5 to 7 minutes; remove bacon and set aside. Add the potatoes to the bacon fat and cook over medium-high heat until browned, about 5 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper. Pour the egg mixture into the skillet, and mix with the potatoes and bacon; allow to cook until eggs are set, 3 to 5 minutes, turning once.

raw_recipe.headline: Bauernomlett (Farmer's Omelet)
raw_recipe.description: Eggs, bacon and potatoes all blend into one dish for a simple breakfast option. Serve it with ketchup for the kids or with a dill pickle for a German-style brunch.

review.reviewBody: This was very good! I did add more ingredients for a more flavorful omelet. I used chopped turkey bacon and leftover red skinned potatoes. I added dried italian herb seasonings and a small amount of fresh shredded cheddar cheese. Tasted great.

Recipe instructions say to cut the potatoes 1/4-inch thick, and then mix with the egg mixture which would break up the potato slices. Makes more sense to me if the potatoes and eggs are to be combined to cube the potatoes, but then it won’t end up looking like an omelet. Awful lot of bacon fat in the skillet, so I did pour out about half of it. I tried to flip it, but the omelette started to break apart, so I just covered it until the eggs were cooked on top. It doesn’t tell you when to add the bacon, so I just sprinkled on after I put the eggs in the skillet. If I were to make this again, I’ll mix the bacon into the egg mixture before it hits the skillet and also add some onion. Cooked this in a 10-inch skillet, and cut in half for 2 servings. Good combo of ingredients which tasted pretty good, but not sure I’ll make again.

bauernfrühstück is what we called it when we lived in Bremen, Germany. Make sure the potatoes a very crispy, so fry them separately with the bacon and onion. Then mix the eggs in a bowl and pour in over the Potatoes to fill in all the little gaps. Add some Paprika with the salt and pepper for color and flavor. Once the eggs are set, serve immediately with a German phrase "Guten Appe" (short for Guten Appetit - Enjoy your meal)

Thank you - very nice change from most breakfasts. After cooking 4 pieces of extra thick bacon, sautéed 1/3 cup of chopped onions, 1/4 cup of chopped red bell pepper and 1 tablespoon of finely chopped hot peppers in the bacon grease. While the potatoes cooked, beat eggs, vegetables, 1 tablespoon of sour cream and 1 tablespoon of cream together. Served with sliced tomatoes. Next time would use less potato or more eggs.
Mixed bacon with the eggs and added some sliced up leftover brats to bacon skillet. Also added mushrooms and some Alpine lace cheese. Tasted great.
I always add an onion and hot.pepper. The potatoes I nuke until semi soft then cut up and finish in the bacon grease along with the pepper and onion.

This was so good and easy! I only used one thin sliced potato, it was enough. I didn’t boil the potato first, just sliced it and fried it in the bacon grease. Then I turned off the burner, crumbled two pieces of bacon on the potato, poured the eggs on top , let them set for a min and put under the broiler for a minute or two to finish setting while my bread toasted. It was enough breakfast for my husband and I. I’ll definitely make this again! Reminds me of a Spanish fritatta without all the work! Thank you!
This receipe is good as is. The great thing about this basic receipe is you can add anything you want and it is good! Very versatile. We have added jalapeno jack cheese for extra kick.
I thought it was called a Dutch omelette. I grew up in Lancaster, Pennsylvania. We always called a Dutch omelette now I know. Lol love it I put garlic and onions in it and sometimes spinach
I’m also using kielbasa thinly sliced. The flavors were wonderful.
A complete breakfast!! Could benefit with some shredded cheddar, I think!

I made this with leftover potatoes cheese a bit of parmesan sharp cheddar and sausage. When in Montana a ranch had a breakfast made of various left over from night before. It was delicious with pieces steak spaghetti and eggs potatoes. I could never copy this alas

It was delicious, but a tad time consuming for what it is. The potatoes really take too much time for this to qualify as a quick meal, BUT— if I ever have leftover boiled potatoes on hand, this recipe is a must make. I did add some onions to sauté with the potatoes.
Ive been cooking this for 40+ years as a New Englander and camping campfire cook. I grew up with it . Its an awesome meal no matter the origin.
Delicious and easy.
This was so delicious thank you for the recipe I will for sure make this often
The best omelette yet
It needs cheese and sausage. Other than that, it's perfect.
This is similar to the omelet I had my first night in Germany. Next time, I'll add some onion and maybe some green pepper. Served with some bread and salad, it would make a nice light meal.
We've made this for years, only we use Spam, and add lots of cheese. The kids and husband love it, and it's a must make when camping!
